comparisons: early vs delayed oral feeding after major gynaecologic surgery
outcomes: ileus; nausea/vomiting; distension/NG tube; bowel recovery; hospital stay; complications; QoL/satisfaction
timepoint_burden: Low; most pooled outcomes are recovery durations or 30-d patient-reported outcomes, not multiple timepoint subgroup analyses
curation_notes: Very manageable report burden and a single perioperative comparison.

comparisons: adrenergic-agonist oral decongestants vs placebo
outcomes: systolic/diastolic BP; heart rate; withdrawals due to AEs
timepoint_burden: Low; short follow-up range, with no major timepoint subgroup axis apparent for the main BP outcomes
curation_notes: Excellent recent first-pass candidate with straightforward continuous outcomes.

comparisons: perineal HAase injection vs placebo injection; HAase vs no intervention
outcomes: perineal trauma; episiotomy; laceration grades; oedema; blood loss; pain; dyspareunia/sexual function
timepoint_burden: Moderate if pain/oedema are curated; main trauma outcomes are simpler, but pain/oedema have separate early follow-up windows
curation_notes: Small and recent; focus first on trauma/episiotomy outcomes.

comparisons: lutein + zeaxanthin vs placebo/no supplementation
outcomes: mortality; ROP; BPD; NEC; sepsis; IVH; neurodevelopment sparse
timepoint_burden: Low; outcomes are mostly neonatal/in-hospital rather than split across multiple meta-analysis time windows
curation_notes: One of the cleanest recent options with standard neonatal binary outcomes.

comparisons: metformin vs megestrol; metformin + megestrol vs megestrol; metformin + LNG-IUS vs LNG-IUS
outcomes: histologic regression; recurrence/progression; hysterectomy; bleeding; QoL; AEs
timepoint_burden: Moderate; review uses short/medium/long timing bins, though many target outcomes cluster around 3-6 mo
curation_notes: Feasible if one comparison branch is chosen first.

review_title: NSAIDs for uncomplicated UTI in women
comparisons: NSAIDs vs antibiotics; antibiotic-sparing strategies
outcomes: symptom resolution; symptom duration; microbiological resolution; pyelonephritis; antibiotic use; AEs
timepoint_burden: Moderate/high; symptom resolution is separated into short- and medium-term windows, with microbiology and AEs at different outcome-specific times
curation_notes: Good recent clinical benchmark; predefine symptom-resolution timing.

review_title: Loop diuretics for acute heart failure
comparisons: continuous infusion vs bolus loop diuretics
outcomes: weight loss/fluid balance; mortality; hospital stay/readmission; AKI; BNP/NT-proBNP; adverse incidents
timepoint_burden: Low/moderate; most outcomes use hospital/discharge or longest follow-up, with readmission timing around 30-90 d
curation_notes: Probably the cleanest first pass: one head-to-head comparison and standard clinical outcomes.

comparisons: antibiotics vs placebo/no intervention; antibiotic vs antibiotic
outcomes: all-cause mortality; serious/non-serious AEs; hospital days
timepoint_burden: Low/moderate; generally maximum follow-up is used, but follow-up differs across trials and is sometimes unclear
curation_notes: Low report burden; comparison branching should be scoped upfront.

comparisons: active vs sham rTMS; standalone/adjunct variants
outcomes: PTSD severity; serious AEs; response/remission
timepoint_burden: Moderate; PTSD severity is separated into immediate, 1-4 wk, and 4-12 wk follow-up windows
curation_notes: Useful SMD/OR benchmark, but rTMS variants add subgroup decisions.

review_title: Lubricating drops for contact lens discomfort
reports_refs_summary: about 10 refs/records; one study without usable outcome data
comparisons: lubricating drops/saline vs no treatment; lubricating drops vs saline
outcomes: contact lens discomfort; end-of-day comfort; dryness; CLDEQ symptoms; ocular signs; AEs
timepoint_burden: Low; short 1-4 wk trials with no obvious multi-timepoint subgroup burden
curation_notes: Compact and recent; two comparator families are the main scoping choice.

comparisons: magnesium sulfate vs placebo/no magnesium for women at risk of preterm birth
outcomes: cerebral palsy; death or cerebral palsy; neurodevelopmental disability; maternal serious outcomes
timepoint_burden: High for neurodevelopmental outcomes; neonatal, 2-yr corrected-age, and school-age follow-up reports may need separate handling
curation_notes: Simple comparison, but child follow-up publications add linkage burden.

comparisons: drospirenone/EE COC vs placebo; one active-COC comparison
outcomes: premenstrual symptoms; functional impairment; mood/physical symptoms; withdrawals; AEs
timepoint_burden: Moderate; cycle-level symptom scores require consistent end-of-treatment timing choices, even if not many formal timepoint subgroups
curation_notes: Symptom scales, cycle timing, and secondary reports add inspection.

comparisons: calcium vs placebo; vitamin D vs placebo; calcium + vitamin D vs placebo
outcomes: hip and lumbar-spine BMD; withdrawals; fractures/adverse events mostly unavailable
timepoint_burden: Low; BMD outcomes are mostly around 12 mo, with limited 6-12 mo timing variation
curation_notes: Low report burden, but three branches and surrogate outcomes.

comparisons: aspirin treatment after desensitisation vs placebo; dosage variants
outcomes: HRQoL/SNOT; asthma control; nasal polyp score; smell; rescue medication; AEs
timepoint_burden: Moderate; main results center on 6 mo, but one long-term 36-mo study may require separate scoping
curation_notes: Recent and small, but sparse outcomes make timing choices important.

comparisons: daratumumab + backbone vs same backbone; VMP, Rd, VCd variants
outcomes: OS; PFS; QoL; mortality; serious AEs; grade 3+ infections
timepoint_burden: Moderate/high; key outcomes use different fixed times, including OS 36 mo, PFS 24 mo, QoL 3/9/12 mo, and longest follow-up harms
curation_notes: Only 4 RCTs, but publication linkage is complicated enough to handle after simpler first-pass reviews.

comparisons: Class I/III antiarrhythmics vs control/placebo/usual care after ablation
outcomes: atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence; hospitalisation; thromboembolism; MI; mortality; repeat ablation; AEs
timepoint_burden: High; recurrence and several safety outcomes are explicitly stratified into 0-3 mo, >3-6 mo, and >6 mo windows
curation_notes: Clean linkage, but timepoint-stratified recurrence is heavier.

comparisons: vitamin B12 supplementation vs placebo/no B12, often with standard co-supplements
outcomes: maternal/infant B12 status; anaemia; birth outcomes; infant growth/neurocognitive and immune outcomes
timepoint_burden: High; maternal, delivery/postpartum, and infant follow-up windows span from pregnancy through multi-year child outcomes
curation_notes: Small trial count, but maternal-child follow-up raises workload.

comparisons: omega-3 PUFA vs placebo
outcomes: self-reported depression symptoms; remission; attrition; AEs
timepoint_burden: Low/moderate; primary meta-analysis appears end-of-treatment, but secondary longer follow-up reports can complicate source matching
curation_notes: Simple comparison, but psychiatric scales and secondary reports add friction.

reports_refs_summary: at least 87 trial refs; 33 author data contacts
comparisons: corticosteroids vs placebo/usual care; continuous infusion vs bolus
outcomes: 28-day, long-term, and hospital mortality; ICU/hospital stay; superinfection; muscle weakness
timepoint_burden: High; mortality and organ-support outcomes are separated across 28-d, 90-d, hospital, long-term, and day-specific windows
curation_notes: Scale stress test with author-provided data and many timepoint analyses.

comparisons: exercise vs attention/placebo; exercise vs usual/no care/education; added exercise vs cointervention alone
outcomes: pain; physical function; QoL; adverse events
timepoint_burden: High; immediate post-intervention and longer follow-up/sustainability windows are important meta-analysis axes
curation_notes: Largest heterogeneity test: many records, scales, and exercise variants.

comparisons: permanent mesh vs native tissue; absorbable mesh vs native tissue; biological graft vs native tissue; mesh/graft variants
outcomes: prolapse awareness/recurrence; repeat surgery; bladder injury; mesh exposure; de novo SUI
timepoint_burden: High; follow-up windows vary by comparison and device/graft type, so outcome timing must be selected deliberately
curation_notes: Strong surgical benchmark, but device/graft variants multiply targets.

review_title: DASH dietary pattern for CVD prevention
comparisons: DASH vs usual/no/minimal/alternative diet interventions across three comparison families
outcomes: CVD events; BP; lipids; glucose/insulin; weight/BMI; QoL; adherence; AEs
timepoint_burden: Moderate/high; lifestyle outcomes span roughly 12 wk to 12 mo, with longer secondary reports that may need separate exclusion or scoping
curation_notes: Relevant and recent, but diet comparators plus secondary reports are slow.

review_title: Digital technology for cystic fibrosis infections
comparisons: digital symptom diary/spirometry monitoring vs routine care
outcomes: exacerbation detection/count; QoL; lung function; hospitalisations; IV antibiotics; microbiology; costs; AEs
timepoint_burden: Low for completed studies; endpoints are mostly 12 mo/52 wk, but limited pooling is the bigger issue
curation_notes: Small study count is misleading; limited pooling and many refs.

review_title: Home versus hospital IV anti-cancer therapy
comparisons: home IV therapy vs hospital outpatient clinic; one study also GP surgery
outcomes: AEs; admissions/attendance; IV-line complications; preference; cost/cost-effectiveness; QoL; satisfaction; adherence
timepoint_burden: Moderate; outcomes use different trial-specific follow-up windows, but setting/economic design issues are bigger than formal timepoint subgroups
curation_notes: Cross-over designs, preferences, and economic outcomes add complexity.

review_title: Steroid injection for carpal tunnel syndrome
comparisons: local corticosteroid injection vs placebo
outcomes: symptoms/function; neurophysiology/imaging; surgery; QoL; AEs
timepoint_burden: High; symptoms/function and neurophysiology are split into <=3 mo and >3 mo, while surgery is assessed up to 12 mo
curation_notes: Clear intervention, but moderate report burden and multiple timepoints.

comparisons: CBT without antipsychotics vs no specific/standard care; antipsychotics; CBT + antipsychotics
outcomes: overall/specific symptoms; relapse; service use; leaving early; functioning; QoL; antipsychotic uptake; AEs/mortality
timepoint_burden: Moderate/high; short, medium, and long follow-up categories are part of the evidence structure
curation_notes: Low study count, but high article count and comparator contamination.
